summary.en: Different paths to entrepreneurship, support around you, and pulling everything together into your own plan.
summary.bs: Različiti putevi do preduzetništva, podrška oko tebe i spajanje svega u tvoj vlastiti plan.

en.one: Social entrepreneurship is running a business whose main goal is solving a social or environmental problem, while still earning its own income.
en.explain: Unlike a charity, a social enterprise sells products or services. Unlike a normal business, profit is a tool, not the main goal; it's often reinvested in the mission. Examples include employing people who struggle to find work, or turning waste into products.
en.example: A café in Tuzla employs young people with disabilities, trains them as baristas, and reinvests profits into opening a second location.
en.why: It shows that business can be a powerful way to make lasting change, not only donations.
en.mixup: A social enterprise still needs a working business model. Good intentions don't pay rent.

bs.one: Social entrepreneurship (društveno preduzetništvo) je vođenje biznisa čiji je glavni cilj rješavanje društvenog ili ekološkog problema, uz to da i dalje zarađuje vlastiti prihod.
bs.explain: Za razliku od humanitarne organizacije, društveno preduzeće prodaje proizvode ili usluge. Za razliku od običnog biznisa, dobit je alat, a ne glavni cilj; često se ponovo ulaže u misiju. Primjeri su zapošljavanje ljudi kojima je teško naći posao ili pretvaranje otpada u proizvode.
bs.example: Kafić u Tuzli zapošljava mlade s invaliditetom, obučava ih za barmene i dobit ulaže u otvaranje druge lokacije.
bs.why: Pokazuje da biznis može biti moćan način za trajnu promjenu, a ne samo donacije.
bs.mixup: Društvenom preduzeću ipak treba poslovni model koji radi. Dobre namjere ne plaćaju zakup.

en.one: A family business is owned and usually run by members of one family, often across generations.
en.explain: Family firms have strong trust, long-term thinking and commitment. Typical challenges are mixing family and business roles, choosing a successor, fair treatment of family members who work and those who don't, and bringing in outside talent.
en.example: A family-owned bakery is passed from father to daughter. Before the handover, they agree in writing on her role, her brother's share as a non-working owner, and a 2-year transition.
en.why: Most businesses in our region are family businesses; managing them well protects both the firm and the family.
en.mixup: Family members aren't automatically the best managers. Successful family firms hire and promote on ability, including outside the family.

bs.one: Family business (porodični biznis) je u vlasništvu i obično pod upravom članova jedne porodice, često kroz generacije.
bs.explain: Porodične firme imaju snažno povjerenje, dugoročno razmišljanje i posvećenost. Tipični izazovi su miješanje porodičnih i poslovnih uloga, izbor nasljednika, pravedan odnos prema članovima porodice koji rade i onima koji ne rade, te dovođenje vanjskih talenata.
bs.example: Porodična pekara prelazi s oca na kćerku. Prije primopredaje pismeno se dogovore o njenoj ulozi, udjelu njenog brata kao vlasnika koji ne radi u firmi i prelaznom periodu od 2 godine.
bs.why: Većina biznisa u regiji su porodični; dobro upravljanje njima štiti i firmu i porodicu.
bs.mixup: Članovi porodice nisu automatski najbolji menadžeri. Uspješne porodične firme zapošljavaju i unapređuju po sposobnosti, i izvan porodice.

en.one: The start-up ecosystem is the network of organisations that support new businesses: incubators, accelerators, co-working spaces, mentors, investors and development agencies.
en.explain: Incubators help very early ideas over a longer time, often with cheap office space and advice. Accelerators run short, intense programmes (around 3 months) for start-ups with a product, often in exchange for a small share and ending with a pitch to investors. Local development agencies and chambers of commerce also offer free advice and training.
en.example: A young team joins a regional accelerator, gets 20.000 € for 6%, three months of mentoring, and pitches to 40 investors on demo day.
en.why: Using the ecosystem saves you from learning everything the hard way, alone.
en.mixup: Joining a programme isn't success in itself. The value comes from using the mentors and contacts actively.

bs.one: Start-up ecosystem (ekosistem za start-upe) je mreža organizacija koje podržavaju nove biznise: inkubatori, akceleratori, co-working prostori, mentori, investitori i razvojne agencije.
bs.explain: Inkubatori pomažu sasvim ranim idejama kroz duži period, često s jeftinim prostorom i savjetima. Akceleratori vode kratke, intenzivne programe (oko 3 mjeseca) za start-upe s proizvodom, često u zamjenu za mali udio, a završavaju predstavljanjem investitorima. Lokalne razvojne agencije i privredne komore takođe nude besplatne savjete i obuke.
bs.example: Mladi tim uđe u regionalni akcelerator, dobije 20.000 € za 6%, tri mjeseca mentorstva i predstavi se pred 40 investitora na demo danu.
bs.why: Korištenje ekosistema te štedi od učenja svega na teži način, sam.
bs.mixup: Ulazak u program sam po sebi nije uspjeh. Vrijednost dolazi od aktivnog korištenja mentora i kontakata.

en.one: Intrapreneurship is acting like an entrepreneur inside an existing company: spotting opportunities, building new products or improving processes, using the company's resources.
en.explain: Intrapreneurs take ownership, test ideas and push change, but with less personal financial risk than founders. Good companies encourage it with time, small budgets and freedom to try things.
en.example: An employee at a bank notices small businesses struggle with loan applications. She proposes and leads a simplified online application that becomes a new product line.
en.why: You can build entrepreneurial skills and impact without leaving your job.
en.mixup: Intrapreneurship isn't doing whatever you want. You still need to work within the company's goals and win support from others.

bs.one: Intrapreneurship (unutrašnje preduzetništvo) je ponašanje kao preduzetnik unutar postojeće firme: uočavanje prilika, pravljenje novih proizvoda ili poboljšanje procesa, uz korištenje resursa firme.
bs.explain: Intrapreneuri preuzimaju odgovornost, testiraju ideje i guraju promjene, ali s manjim ličnim finansijskim rizikom od osnivača. Dobre firme to podstiču vremenom, malim budžetima i slobodom da se probaju stvari.
bs.example: Zaposlenica u banci primijeti da se mali biznisi muče sa zahtjevima za kredit. Predloži i vodi pojednostavljen online zahtjev koji postane nova linija proizvoda.
bs.why: Možeš razvijati preduzetničke vještine i uticaj bez napuštanja posla.
bs.mixup: Unutrašnje preduzetništvo nije raditi šta god hoćeš. I dalje trebaš raditi u okviru ciljeva firme i pridobiti podršku drugih.

en.one: An exit strategy is the founder's plan for how they will eventually leave the business and turn their ownership into money, or hand it over.
en.explain: Options include selling to another company or a buyer, selling to employees or managers, passing it to family, listing on a stock exchange, or simply closing it in an orderly way. Thinking about the exit early shapes decisions about structure, records and dependence on the founder.
en.example: A founder who built an IT support firm over 15 years spends three years making it run without him, then sells it to a larger competitor at a good price.
en.why: A business that can run and be sold without you is worth much more.
en.mixup: Planning an exit doesn't mean you want to leave soon. It means you're building something with value beyond yourself.

bs.one: Exit strategy (strategija izlaska) je plan osnivača kako će jednom napustiti biznis i pretvoriti svoje vlasništvo u novac ili ga predati.
bs.explain: Opcije su prodaja drugoj firmi ili kupcu, prodaja radnicima ili menadžerima, prenošenje na porodicu, izlazak na berzu, ili jednostavno uredno zatvaranje. Razmišljanje o izlasku rano oblikuje odluke o strukturi, evidenciji i zavisnosti od osnivača.
bs.example: Osnivač koji je 15 godina gradio firmu za IT podršku provede tri godine praveći je da radi bez njega, a zatim je proda većem konkurentu po dobroj cijeni.
bs.why: Biznis koji može raditi i biti prodan bez tebe vrijedi mnogo više.
bs.mixup: Planiranje izlaska ne znači da želiš uskoro otići. Znači da gradiš nešto s vrijednošću izvan sebe.

concepts.youtubeQuery: how to start a business step by step beginner

en.one: Putting it all together means combining what you've learned across the programmes into one simple, testable plan for your own venture.
en.explain: A practical path: pick a problem you understand (founder-market fit), talk to 20 potential customers, sketch a Lean Canvas, check the numbers (costs, margin, break-even, runway), test with an MVP or pre-sales, choose the right legal form and register, then measure traction and adjust.
en.example: Mo's own test: choose one idea, fill a Lean Canvas in an evening, run five customer interviews this month, and set a 'go / change / stop' decision date in 90 days.
en.why: Knowledge only becomes useful when you apply it to a real decision.
en.mixup: You don't need a perfect plan to start. You need a small, clear next step and a way to learn from it.

bs.one: Sve na jednom mjestu znači spojiti ono što si naučio kroz programe u jedan jednostavan plan koji se može testirati, za tvoj vlastiti poduhvat.
bs.explain: Praktičan put: izaberi problem koji razumiješ (usklađenost osnivača i tržišta), razgovaraj s 20 potencijalnih kupaca, skiciraj Lean Canvas, provjeri brojeve (troškovi, marža, tačka pokrića, rezerva), testiraj s MVP-om ili prodajom unaprijed, izaberi pravi pravni oblik i registruj se, zatim mjeri traciju i prilagođavaj.
bs.example: Mo-ov vlastiti test: izaberi jednu ideju, popuni Lean Canvas za jedno veče, obavi pet razgovora s kupcima ovog mjeseca i postavi datum odluke 'nastavi / promijeni / stani' za 90 dana.
bs.why: Znanje postaje korisno tek kad ga primijeniš na stvarnu odluku.
bs.mixup: Ne treba ti savršen plan da počneš. Treba ti mali, jasan sljedeći korak i način da iz njega učiš.

q.en: What makes a social enterprise different from a charity?
q.bs: Šta razlikuje društveno preduzeće od humanitarne organizacije?

options.en: It earns income by selling products or services

explain.en: Social enterprises fund their mission through trading.
explain.bs: Društvena preduzeća finansiraju misiju kroz prodaju.

q.en: A short, intense 3-month programme that ends with a demo day is…
q.bs: Kratak, intenzivan program od 3 mjeseca koji završava demo danom je…

explain.en: Accelerators are short and intense; incubators are longer and earlier.
explain.bs: Akceleratori su kratki i intenzivni; inkubatori su duži i za raniju fazu.

q.en: Why does a good exit strategy raise a business's value?
q.bs: Zašto dobra strategija izlaska povećava vrijednost biznisa?

options.en: The business can run without the founder

explain.en: Buyers pay more for firms that don't depend on one person.
explain.bs: Kupci plaćaju više za firme koje ne zavise od jedne osobe.

q.en: What's the best first step after learning all this?
q.bs: Koji je najbolji prvi korak nakon što sve ovo naučiš?

options.en: A small, clear test with real customers
options.bs: Mali, jasan test sa stvarnim kupcima

explain.en: Start small, learn fast, then decide.
explain.bs: Počni malo, uči brzo, pa odluči.
